cards.text: Last chapter, Wisdom stood out in the street YELLING for anybody who'd listen (Prov 1:20). Now a father sits his son down and opens with one little word: IF. If you accept my words, he says, and friend, he is just getting warmed up.

cards.question: If the son accepts his father's words, what should he do with his father's commandments?

answers.text: Read them aloud at the gate

cards.text: And the IFs keep stacking up: turn your ear to wisdom, point your heart at understanding. This man writes instructions like a recipe card, and he is NOT on the last step yet.

cards.question: When it comes to insight, the son is told to truly call out to it. He's told to lift his ___ to understanding.

cards.text: Back in chapter 1, Wisdom lifted her voice in the street (Prov 1:20). Now the son is told to lift his right back. Friend, that's not a lecture anymore, that's a CONVERSATION.

cards.question: The father paints a picture of how hard to look for wisdom. He says to search for it the way people search for what?

answers.text: A lost coin and a lost sheep

cards.text: Seek it like silver, search it out like hidden treasure. That is not a casual look, friend, that's flipping every couch cushion for your car keys when you are ALREADY LATE.

cards.question: All those IFs lead to one big THEN. If the son seeks wisdom like treasure, what does he discover?

cards.text: Now here's the twist. The son does all that digging, but he doesn't make the treasure. He just brings the shovel.

cards.question: The son does the searching, but the ___ is the one who gives wisdom.

cards.text: The LORD stores up sound wisdom for the upright, like a cookie box set aside with your name on it. And He's not just the giver, friend, He's a protector too.

cards.question: To those who walk with integrity, the LORD is a ___.
The LORD guards the paths of justice and protects the way of His saints.

cards.text: And here comes ANOTHER then. Then you will discern, he says, the same three words he used back in verse 5, because this dad does not waste a good line.

cards.question: This time the father says the son will discern every good path. Which ones does he name?

cards.text: Wisdom doesn't just knock on the door, friend. It walks right into the son's heart, unpacks its bags and puts its toothbrush by the sink.

cards.question: Once wisdom enters the son's heart, knowledge will feel like a heavy load on his soul.
With wisdom moved into the son's heart, what will watch over him and guard him?

cards.text: Discretion and understanding aren't standing guard for decoration, friend. They're there to deliver the son from the way of evil and from the man who speaks perversity.
These folks leave the straight paths to walk in the ways of darkness. Friend, I spent YEARS in a dark junk drawer trying to get out, and these people are walking IN?!

cards.question: The people who walk in the ways of darkness feel guilty every time they do evil.
The people who leave the straight paths walk paths that are ___ and ways that are devious.

cards.text: Wisdom will also rescue the son from the forbidden woman, the stranger with seductive words. She has walked away from the partner of her youth.

cards.question: Besides walking away from the partner of her youth, what does the forbidden woman forget?

answers.text: The way back to her city

cards.text: Then the father gets very serious about where her house leads. No jokes on this card, friend. Lean in.

cards.question: Where does the forbidden woman's house sink?
People who go to the forbidden woman can come back and find the paths of life again.

cards.text: So where does all this guarding leave the son? On the right road, friend, and nowhere near that crooked crowd.

cards.question: With wisdom guarding him, the son will follow in the ways of the ___ and keep to the paths of the righteous.

cards.text: The father closes with two groups of people and two very different endings. Friend, this is the part where you want to be in the FIRST group.

cards.question: What happens to the upright and the blameless?

answers.text: They inhabit the land and remain in it
They leave the land for a far country
They rule over the land as kings

cards.question: The wicked and the unfaithful will remain in the land alongside the upright.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to guess the wording of the second half of 2:1 ('hide my commandments within you'). Nothing on card 1 lets a baker reason toward 'hide them within him' over the other two answers, so this is a luck pick on the exact wording of a line. It also turns the father's 'if' into a 'should.'

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: This is a recap card. 2:3 was just asked on card 4, and this card restates it without moving the passage forward.

The card says Wisdom 'lifted her voice in the street,' but Prov 1:20 says she calls out in the street and lifts her voice in the square. It also links 1:20 and 2:3 into a 'CONVERSATION' between the son and Wisdom, which neither text states.

rule.text: When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: This is a recap card. It repeats 2:4 ('Seek it like silver, search it out like hidden treasure') right after card 6 asked it, and adds only a joke. The joke should ride on a card that moves the passage forward.
'He's a protector too' gives away card 12's answer, 'shield.' It also rules out the wrong answers 'teacher' and 'witness,' since neither is a protector.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card quotes 'Then you will discern' and calls it 'the same three words' from verse 5. The phrase it gives is four words, so what he points out isn't accurate.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The question asks which 'good paths' are named. Only the right answer (righteousness, justice, equity) is a set of virtues or paths. 'The times and the seasons' and 'The dreams of the king' are a different kind of thing, so the question rules them out and the right answer stands out. Card 13 also already showed 'paths of justice.'

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.

findings.problem: The joke says he spent years in the junk drawer 'trying to get out.' His backstory says he gave up, lay in the dark and waited for the drawer to open. Trying to get out adds something new to his story that doesn't fit it.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: BSB 2:16 says 'It will rescue you.' The card names the subject as 'Wisdom,' which settles what the text leaves open. 'It' could point back to discretion and understanding (2:11-12) or to wisdom (2:10).

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Most story cards in stop 2 (cards 5, 10 and 12) read as plain narration or a pleasant dad line, with no real laugh. The serious moment on card 7 is fine. The lighter cards around it should push for genuine humor.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
